extracted.intended_audience: journalism researchers, media scholars, journalism educators, and media professionals
extracted.subtask_description: A cross-national comparative survey study examining journalists' role perceptions, epistemological orientations, and ethical views across 18 countries (n≈1,800). The page summarizes key normative/valuational dimensions of professional journalism identified by the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role perceptions, epistemological orientations and ethical views
rubrics_metrics.description: This article reports key findings from a comparative survey of the role perceptions, epistemological orientations and ethical views of 1800 journalists from 18 countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as the overarching dimensions the study measures; the subsequent criteria (detachment, impartiality, interventionism, etc.) are specific components of these broad categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Detachment ... are considered essential journalistic functions around the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a widely valued role norm internationally, though the perceived importance of detachment varies across countries and cultural contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-involvement ... are considered essential journalistic functions around the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely related to detachment; treated as a normative expectation for journalists in many countries but with cross-national variation in endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing political information
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing political information ... are considered essential journalistic functions around the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Viewed as a core function of journalism worldwide — emphasis on informing the public about political matters as a professional obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring the government
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitoring the government ... are considered essential journalistic functions around the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a watchdog role valued across countries; importance varies by national context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Impartiality ... are also valued worldwide, though their perceived importance varies across countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality is presented as a commonly held ethical standard; degree of adherence and emphasis differs between western and non-western contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability and factualness of information
rubrics_metrics.description: The reliability and factualness of information ... are also valued worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic quality criteria emphasizing accurate, fact-based reporting; universally recognized but variably prioritized across countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to universal ethical principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to universal ethical principles are also valued worldwide, though their perceived importance varies across countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study contrasts commitment to universalist ethics (more typical among western journalists) with contextual or flexible ethical approaches in other regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventionism
rubrics_metrics.description: Various aspects of interventionism ... seem to play out differently around the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interventionism (the degree to which journalists actively promote values, ideas or social change) is a contested role norm: western journalists tend to be less supportive, non-western journalists tend to be more interventionist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivism
rubrics_metrics.description: Various aspects of ... objectivism ... seem to play out differently around the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectivism as an epistemological orientation (belief in objective, value-free reporting) varies cross-nationally in its endorsement and operationalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separating facts from opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of separating facts from opinion ... seem to play out differently around the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on a clear boundary between factual reporting and opinion varies by country; some journalists prioritize strict separation while others allow more blending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active promotion of particular values, ideas and social change
rubrics_metrics.description: Western journalists are generally less supportive of any active promotion of particular values, ideas and social change, and they adhere more to universal principles in their ethical decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames advocacy or explicit value-promotion as a role dimension; the study finds systematic regional differences in support for this practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility versus universalism in ethical decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists from non-western contexts ... tend to be more interventionist in their role perceptions and more flexible in their ethical views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts two ethical orientations: adherence to universal ethical principles (more common in western contexts) versus situational/ flexible ethics (more common in non-western contexts); useful for evaluating normative claims about journalistic behavior.
